name: OSS Goldmine
positioning: Daily opportunity radar for builders and their AI agents

cards.why_now: Teams using headless browsers often discover runaway jobs, flaky sessions, and expensive retries too late.
cards.target_user: growth, QA, and data teams running browser automation
cards.first_test: Monitor job duration, retries, and failures, then flag the top expensive automation patterns.
cards.risk: Needs access to real automation logs.
cards.do_not_build: Do not build another browser automation platform.
cards.agent_prompt: Turn this into a 3-day build plan for a tiny browser automation cost report.

cards.why_now: Internal docs go stale quietly, and teams only notice after onboarding, support, or operations break.
cards.target_user: remote teams relying on internal knowledge bases
cards.first_test: Scan pages for old owners, stale dates, duplicate instructions, and missing update signals.
cards.risk: Needs integrations with real knowledge-base permissions.
cards.do_not_build: Do not build a full wiki or knowledge-base replacement.
cards.agent_prompt: Turn this into a small freshness report workflow for one exported knowledge base.

cards.why_now: Automation tools are powerful, but debugging failed workflows still eats founder and ops time.
cards.target_user: ops teams running no-code or low-code automations
cards.first_test: Turn failed workflow logs into plain-English causes and suggested fixes.
cards.risk: Many failures are integration-specific and need good fixtures.
cards.do_not_build: Do not build a new automation platform.
cards.agent_prompt: Turn this into a log-to-explanation prototype using sample failed workflow runs.

cards.why_now: Old API testing teams still need a painless way to move collections, compare responses, and avoid breaking workflows.
cards.target_user: API-heavy dev teams leaving legacy tools
cards.first_test: Build a tiny importer that compares two collections and exports a migration report.
cards.risk: High competition in the API client market.
cards.do_not_build: Do not build a full API client.
cards.agent_prompt: Turn this into a 3-day build plan for a migration diff report.

cards.why_now: React apps keep getting slower, but most teams do not want to live inside profiler traces.
cards.first_test: Turn profiling output into a shareable before-and-after performance report.
cards.do_not_build: Do not build a full browser devtool replacement.
cards.agent_prompt: Turn this into a report-first React performance prototype.

cards.opportunity: A branded API docs handoff kit
cards.why_now: Teams need polished API docs, but customizing and handing them to non-engineers is still messy.
cards.target_user: B2B teams exposing APIs to customers
cards.first_test: Generate a hosted docs preview plus a handoff checklist from one OpenAPI file.
cards.risk: Customization needs can become too broad.
cards.do_not_build: Do not build a full API documentation platform.
cards.agent_prompt: Turn this into a one-file OpenAPI docs handoff prototype.

cards.why_now: Many products depend on PDFs, but teams still manually check rendering, forms, and export quality.
cards.target_user: ops-heavy SaaS teams handling contracts, invoices, and reports
cards.first_test: Compare expected fields, screenshot pages, and flag broken exports for one PDF workflow.
cards.risk: PDF edge cases can explode quickly.
cards.do_not_build: Do not build a general PDF editor.
cards.agent_prompt: Turn this into a PDF export QA checklist and screenshot prototype.

cards.why_now: Component libraries grow fast, but teams rarely know which stories, props, and screenshots drifted.
cards.target_user: frontend platform teams with shared component libraries
cards.first_test: Scan Storybook metadata and produce a weekly drift report for component owners.
cards.risk: May overlap with visual regression and design-system tooling.
cards.do_not_build: Do not build a full Storybook alternative.
cards.agent_prompt: Turn this into a metadata-only drift report before visual diffing.

cards.why_now: Legacy debugging tools still attract attention, but the safer opportunity is helping teams move to modern defaults.
cards.first_test: Package a migration guide plus automated config checks for VS Code and Chrome DevTools.
cards.risk: Likely obsolete if official tooling already covers most needs.
cards.agent_prompt: Turn this into a migration checklist, not a new debugger.

cards.why_now: API workspaces become messy, duplicated, and impossible to hand over after a few sprints.
cards.target_user: small dev teams with growing API collections
cards.first_test: Detect duplicate requests, stale environment variables, and missing examples in one workspace.
cards.risk: Needs import/export support from target API tools.
cards.do_not_build: Do not build a new API client.
cards.agent_prompt: Turn this into a cleanup report for one exported API workspace.
